en.title: Schubert, String Quartet in D minor, D.810 – IV. Presto: A Listening Guide
en.overview: This finale is in 6/8 and starts in D minor. It has four parts: Part 1 (repeated), Part 2 (repeated), a very long Part 3, and a closing Prestissimo, which means "extremely fast". Listen for the main theme. It comes back many times, often with several instruments playing it together. Listen also for sudden jumps between very soft and very loud. Keys and chords here are estimated by computer, so treat the key labels as a guide.

listening_points.headline: The main theme, soft and together
listening_points.text: The movement opens softly in D minor with the main theme [m. 0-2]. Violin 1 probably leads, but Violin 2 plays the same notes and the cello plays them an octave lower. The instruments play in unison or octaves, so it sounds like one strong line. The theme is heard again at [m. 8-10].

listening_points.headline: A sudden hush and a brighter key
listening_points.text: At [m. 13] the music drops suddenly to very soft. No gradual change is marked. By [m. 15-16] the estimated key moves to B-flat major, which sounds a little brighter. Part 1 is marked to be repeated.

listening_points.headline: Part 2 begins with the viola
listening_points.text: Part 2 starts with a solo viola at [m. 16]. The viola then carries the main theme in F major [m. 16-18]. The others accompany it softly. This is the first time the theme moves to a new key.

listening_points.headline: A swell in A major to full force
listening_points.text: In A major the music swells from soft [m. 25], because a crescendo (getting louder) is marked. It reaches loud at [m. 29] and very loud at [m. 31]. Then it drops suddenly to soft at [m. 32]. The instruments move together in block-like chords.

listening_points.headline: Back to D minor, then a loud theme in F major
listening_points.text: The main theme returns in D minor [m. 34-36], with the viola and cello playing it. The music then drops to very soft [m. 37-41]. At [m. 42] it jumps suddenly to loud. The theme is then played in F major by both violins and the cello [m. 42-44].

listening_points.headline: D major: loud and soft trade places
listening_points.text: The estimated key turns to D major, which sounds brighter. Loud and soft alternate quickly [m. 47-58]. At [m. 51] and [m. 56] a diminuendo (getting softer) is marked. The end of Part 2 is very loud [m. 59-62a], then it drops to soft at [m. 63b]. Part 2 is repeated.

listening_points.headline: Part 3 starts: a swell, then a solo violin
listening_points.text: Part 3 is the long central section. At [m. 65] the estimated key turns to A major, and the music swells. Loud chords arrive at [m. 67]. Violin 1 plays alone at [m. 68]. This pattern of a loud chord followed by a solo line repeats at [m. 69-70].

listening_points.headline: A drop to near silence, then a blast
listening_points.text: The music drops to very soft at [m. 85] and then to very, very soft at [m. 87]. These are sudden changes, not gradual ones. At [m. 88] every instrument is silent. Then at [m. 90] the music bursts in at very loud, with no warning.

listening_points.headline: Loud, driving chords with sharp accents
listening_points.text: Violin 1 probably carries the top line while all four play loud chords. Many beats carry an fz accent, a sharp, forceful attack. The estimated key moves from F major through C major to A major, with no break in the loudness.

listening_points.headline: Low strings take the tune
listening_points.text: The tune moves down. The cello probably leads at [m. 112-116]. After that the viola probably takes over [m. 117-123]. Both guesses are uncertain. The music is still very loud, and the others accompany.

listening_points.headline: Soft again: a solo violin, then a hush
listening_points.text: After a diminuendo marked at [m. 127], the music is soft at [m. 131]. Violin 1 plays alone in [m. 132-134]. Then the music goes very soft in F major [m. 135]. Violin 1 leads with the others accompanying.

listening_points.headline: Violin 2 leads a quiet stretch
listening_points.text: For a long, very soft stretch Violin 2 probably has the melody [m. 175-191], with the others accompanying. A diminuendo is marked at [m. 189] and [m. 191]. The estimated key then darkens to E minor [m. 193].

listening_points.headline: E major: loud accents, then sudden calm
listening_points.text: At [m. 205] the music jumps to very loud. It stays in E major with sharp fz accents [m. 206-212]. Then it drops suddenly to soft at [m. 213].

listening_points.headline: A long, quiet, wandering stretch
listening_points.text: The music stays very soft and shifts through several estimated keys: G minor, C-sharp minor, then E major [m. 316-317]. Violin 1 is in a solo texture for much of [m. 311-318]. The mood is uneasy and hovering before the theme returns.

listening_points.headline: The opening theme comes home
listening_points.text: At [m. 319] the main theme returns in D minor, played together by both violins and the cello [m. 319-321]. It sits at the same pitch as the very opening. It comes back softly. The viola then has the theme in F major [m. 335-337], just as in Part 2.

listening_points.headline: One more return of the theme
listening_points.text: The main theme returns again in D minor at [m. 653], softly. Both violins and the cello play it, again at the pitch of the opening [m. 653-655]. It repeats at [m. 661-663]. Then the theme appears in A major and in D minor again at [m. 685-689].

listening_points.headline: Prestissimo: a rush to the end
listening_points.text: The final section starts very soft [m. 709]. The analysis marks measure 749 as the loudest and busiest point (very loud). But the score marks fff, louder still, at [m. 754], so this estimate is rough. The movement ends in D minor [m. 755].

glossary.explanation: A tune you can recognise when it comes back. Here it is the main theme from the first bar.
The home note and mood of a stretch of music. Minor keys often sound darker and major keys brighter.
A move from one key to another.
Instruments play the same tune together, at the same pitch or an octave apart.
All parts move together in chords, with the top line as the tune.
One part has the tune while the others play a supporting background.
No instrument plays in that measure.
A sharp, forceful accent on a note or chord.
Extremely fast. It is the marking for the closing section.
Loudness levels. p is soft, pp very soft, f loud, ff very loud, fff louder still.

zh.title: 舒伯特 D小调弦乐四重奏（D.810）第四乐章 Presto 听赏指南
zh.overview: 这是一首6/8拍、速度很快的终乐章，主调是D小调。乐章从一个轻声的主旋律开始，之后在许多不同的调之间游走，主旋律一再回来。最后是一段标为 Prestissimo（更快）的尾声。请留意：谁在拉旋律、声音忽强忽弱，以及主旋律回来的时刻。本指南中的调和和弦都是电脑自动估计的，仅供参考。

listening_points.headline: 轻声开场：主旋律齐奏
listening_points.text: 乐章以弱奏（p）开始，几个声部以齐奏（相同的音或相差八度）奏出主旋律 [m. 0-2]。主旋律在 [m. 8-10] 又出现一次。从 [m. 13] 起声音更轻，成为很弱（pp）。第一小提琴大概是主导声部，但把握不大。

listening_points.headline: 中提琴先唱主旋律
listening_points.text: 第二部分在 [m. 16] 开始，中提琴先唱出旋律，这一小节是独奏。随后其他乐器加入，以主调织体（旋律与和声同步进行）伴奏 [m. 17-18]。此时调估计为F大调。

listening_points.headline: 渐强到很强，再突然变轻
listening_points.text: [m. 25] 起标有渐强（声音慢慢变响），进入A大调。声音由 p 经 f [m. 29] 到 ff [m. 31]。到 [m. 32] 突然回到 p。

listening_points.headline: 主旋律回到D小调，再转强
listening_points.text: [m. 34] 主旋律回到D小调，由中提琴和大提琴奏出。[m. 37] 突然变成很弱（pp）。到 [m. 42] 突然转强（f），主旋律在F大调出现 [m. 42-44]，之后又回到D小调。

listening_points.headline: 转入D大调，强弱交替
listening_points.text: [m. 46] 起转为D大调，色彩明亮些。声音在 f 和 p 之间来回，[m. 57] 到很弱（pp）。[m. 59-62a] 达到很强（ff），[m. 63b] 又突然回到 p。

listening_points.headline: 第三部分：A大调、F大调、C大调
listening_points.text: 第三部分是全乐章最长的一段，开始就转向A大调 [m. 65]。强弱对比很大：[m. 67] 转强（f），[m. 70] 又变弱（p）。随后调依次转到F大调 [m. 72] 和C大调 [m. 74]。[m. 68] 是第一小提琴独奏。

listening_points.headline: 先变得极轻，然后突然爆发
listening_points.text: [m. 85] 声音突然变得很弱（pp），[m. 87] 更弱（ppp）。[m. 88] 全体休止。[m. 90] 又突然爆发到很强（ff）。谱上没有标记逐步变化，所以这些都是突变。

listening_points.headline: 大提琴、中提琴可能轮流唱旋律
listening_points.text: 这里不再由第一小提琴带头。[m. 112-116] 可能是大提琴领头，[m. 117-120] 可能是中提琴领头，其他声部伴奏。这一判断不太确定。整段都很强（ff）。

listening_points.headline: 安静下来：很弱的长段
listening_points.text: [m. 127] 标有渐弱，[m. 131] 转为弱（p），[m. 132-134] 是第一小提琴独奏。[m. 135] 起变得很弱（pp），第一小提琴带旋律，其他声部伴奏。[m. 149] 起标有渐弱，调转向A小调 [m. 153]。

listening_points.headline: 第二小提琴接过旋律
listening_points.text: [m. 175-191] 第二小提琴大概带着旋律，整段很弱（pp），其他声部伴奏。[m. 189] 与 [m. 191] 标有渐弱。随后调转向E小调 [m. 193]。

listening_points.headline: 调频繁变换，小提琴长段独奏
listening_points.text: [m. 294] 起进入G小调，整段保持很弱（pp）。第一小提琴在 [m. 311-318] 独奏。调在升C小调和G小调之间摇摆 [m. 306-310]，最后到E大调 [m. 316]，随后主旋律回归。

listening_points.headline: 开头主旋律再次回来
listening_points.text: [m. 319] 主旋律回到D小调，音高与开头相同，仍是弱奏（p）和齐奏。[m. 331] 起变为很弱（pp）。[m. 335] 中提琴又在F大调唱出主旋律。这一段与开头很相似。

listening_points.headline: 大提琴与第二小提琴对话
listening_points.text: [m. 399-402] 大提琴大概带着旋律，调转到A大调与升C小调。[m. 403] 起转为很强（ff），第二小提琴领头，调是F小调。这是弱奏和强奏反复对比的一段。

listening_points.headline: 主旋律再次回到D小调
listening_points.text: [m. 653] 起主旋律又回到D小调，音高和开头一致，是弱奏（p）、齐奏。[m. 666] 起转为很弱（pp）。

listening_points.headline: 更快的尾声，冲向最强
listening_points.text: [m. 709] 起进入标为 Prestissimo 的尾声，从很弱（pp）开始，D大调，几个声部齐奏。电脑估计最响最忙处在 [m. 749]（ff）。[m. 754] 起谱上标为更强的 fff，说明这个估计只是粗略的。最后在D小调结束 [m. 744-755]。

glossary.explanation: 几件乐器节奏大体一致，像一起唱和弦。
几件乐器用相同的音（或相差八度）演奏同一条旋律。
声音慢慢变响 / 慢慢变轻。
音乐的“中心调”改变，色彩随之变亮或变暗。大调通常偏明亮，小调偏暗。
很弱 / 弱 / 强 / 很强 / 最强。
意为“比急板还快”，这里是乐章最后的尾声。
